A coordinate plane showing the graph of the quadratic curve y = x^2 - 4x + 3. The curve is a U-shape (parabola) opening upwards. It crosses the x-axis at x = 1 and x = 3, and the y-axis at y = 3. The lowest point (minimum) is marked at the coordinates (2, -1).

A coordinate plane showing the cubic graph y = x^3 - 3x^2. The curve comes from the bottom left, goes up to a local maximum at the origin (0, 0), dips down to a local minimum at (2, -4), and then curves back up to the top right. The x-intercepts are at 0 and 3.
